tickerNote: US & Europe close Tue 10 Nov · India: Mon 9 Nov (markets shut Tue for Diwali Balipratipada)

lead.headline: Hot Inflation Print Halts Wall Street's Rebound and Revives Fed Rate-Hike Talk
lead.deck: October consumer prices ran ahead of forecasts, sending short-term Treasury yields up the most since April 2025 and pulling stocks lower a day after their best session in seven months.
body: US consumer prices rose 0.4% in October, a tenth of a point above economists' forecasts, and core prices excluding food and energy rose 0.3% against an expected 0.2%. The surprise pushed traders to raise their bets that the Federal Reserve will hike rates in December rather than hold.

Bond markets moved first. The two-year Treasury yield jumped about 17 basis points to roughly 4.73%, its biggest one-day rise since April 2025, and the 10-year yield closed near 4.98%. Gold fell about 2.7% to around $4,031 an ounce, and gold-mining shares dropped more than 5%.

Stocks gave back part of Monday's surge, when the S&P 500 rose 2.35% and the Dow gained more than 1,100 points as oil prices fell. On Tuesday the S&P 500 slipped 0.38% to 7,520.93, the Dow lost 0.3% to 52,231.89 and the Nasdaq fell 0.74% to 25,065.87. Technology was the weakest sector, and homebuilders fell on worries about mortgage rates.

Nvidia weighed heavily for a second day, falling about 5.5% as its board investigates chief executive Jensen Huang's relationship with an alleged Chinese spy. Europe largely shrugged off the data as cheaper oil supported shares, while Indian markets were closed for a holiday and reopen today.

top: Hotter-than-expected US inflation sent yields sharply higher and stocks lower; traders now lean toward a December Fed hike.
Nvidia fell about 5.5% for a second straight loss as its board investigates CEO Jensen Huang.
Anthropic revised its IPO plans to a public offering of up to $64.4 billion plus a $26 billion private placement with tech partners.
Germany will reportedly pay €6.6 billion for a 50% stake in tank maker KNDS.
SEBI cleared MakeMyTrip's India listing as Indian markets prepare to reopen after Diwali.

items.headline: October Inflation Overshoots
items.body: Both headline and core US consumer prices beat forecasts by a tenth of a point, reviving expectations of a December Fed rate hike.

items.headline: Treasury Yields Jump Across the Curve
items.body: The two-year yield posted its largest daily gain since April 2025 as traders repriced the Fed outlook.

items.headline: Europe Edges Higher on Cheaper Oil
items.body: Lower crude prices and easing US–Iran tensions kept the Stoxx 600 within two points of its record close; London lagged as energy shares fell.

items.headline: Asia Rebounded Ahead of the Data
items.body: Seoul and Tokyo rallied on Tuesday after Wall Street's strong Monday, recovering part of last week's AI-driven losses. India's markets were closed for Diwali Balipratipada, and the rupee last closed at 93.93 to the dollar on Monday.

items.headline: Nvidia Slides for a Second Day
items.body: An independent board committee is examining CEO Jensen Huang's relationship with an alleged Chinese spy; the company says it has no reason to believe secrets were compromised. Shares are about 31% below their October peak, with earnings due 17 November.

items.headline: Homebuilders Hit by Rising Yields
items.body: Lennar led housing stocks lower as the jump in Treasury yields raised fears of higher mortgage rates.

items.headline: Gold Miners Tumble With Bullion
items.body: Mining shares fell more than 5% as gold dropped sharply after the inflation report.

items.headline: PSU Banks Lead Dalal Street's Monday Gain
items.body: In India's last session, state lenders drove the Nifty PSU Bank index up about 3.7% and the Nifty to its highest close since late February, while metals and IT lagged.

items.headline: Berlin to Buy Into Tank Maker KNDS
items.body: Germany will reportedly pay €6.6 billion for half of the Franco-German defence group from its founding families, with a signing expected this month.

items.headline: EP Group Takes Control of Fnac Darty
items.body: Daniel Křetínský's EP Group now holds 69.3% of the French electronics retailer, and its offer will reopen from 12 to 25 November.

items.headline: Samsung Fire Moves to Own Canopius Outright
items.body: South Korea's Samsung Fire & Marine agreed to buy the rest of the specialty insurer from funds managed by KKR and Korea Investment Corporation.

items.headline: Argenx and Huaxin Strike Deals
items.body: Argenx agreed to buy peptide-drug specialist Unnatural Products for up to $1.15 billion, and China's Huaxin agreed to buy Brazilian CSN's cement unit at a $2.31 billion enterprise value.

items.headline: Stock Pickers Nurse a Historic Rout
items.body: Goldman Sachs data showed fundamental and systematic long/short funds both lost more than 3% in October, a first in its records, and the pain carried into November. Walleye, Engineers Gate and Brevan Howard have cut staff.

items.headline: Citadel Bucks the Trend
items.body: Citadel's flagship Wellington fund was one of the few big multistrategy funds to finish October in positive territory.

items.headline: Millennium Pulls $1.5bn From Two Managers
items.body: After a losing October, Millennium withdrew external capital from Axebrook and Troluce Capital following losses at both firms.

items.headline: Anthropic Resets Its Mega-IPO
items.body: After withdrawing a prospectus with a pricing error, the AI company filed revised terms that pair the public offering with a $26 billion private placement from Google, Nvidia, Microsoft and other tech partners.

items.headline: Barrick Files to List North American Arm
items.body: Barrick Mining filed for a New York IPO of about 10% of American Barrick Gold, which will hold its Nevada mines and Pueblo Viejo.

items.headline: SEBI Clears MakeMyTrip's India Listing
items.body: The regulator approved the travel company's proposed India IPO, structured as an offer for sale by its Nasdaq-listed parent.

items.headline: ShareChat's Losses Widen Despite Growth
items.body: Parent Mohalla Tech's FY26 net loss rose about 79% even as operating revenue grew around 40%. Separately, Indian startups raised about $290 million in the 2–7 November week, led by jewellery D2C brand GIVA.
